name: Johanan
overview: Johanan was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Elioenai. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or events recorded beyond his lineage. This makes him a minor but distinct figure within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Johanan means 'YHWH is gracious,' reflecting a common theophoric element in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's grace. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:24 and was not given directly by God but is significant in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Johanan as the son of Elioenai, establishing his place within the family line. No other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Johanan's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical lineage of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:24. While he does not appear in narrative accounts, his inclusion preserves the continuity of God's covenant people and highlights the faithfulness of God's promises through generations.
